sections.overview: This tiny resident kingfisher inhabits lowland forests of maritime Southeast Asia; modern BirdLife taxonomy treats it as a species distinct from the Black-backed Dwarf Kingfisher (C. erithaca).
sections.identification: It has a bright orange bill and underparts with rufous upperparts; the black-backed species C. erithaca instead shows a dark blue-black back, an important distinction in the former species complex.
sections.habitat: It is associated with lowland forest, often near streams, and is recorded as resident rather than a long-distance migrant.
sections.diet: As a small kingfisher it takes small animal prey; detailed species-specific diet data remain sparse in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: Field observers in Malaysia documented a courting pair and nesting activity in 2023, adding rare observations to a species whose behaviour is little known.
sections.reproduction: The Malaysian observations include courtship and nest records, but the brief report does not establish a range-wide breeding calendar or typical clutch size.
sections.ecology: C. rufidorsa and C. erithaca were repeatedly lumped and split in bird checklists; the split is supported by genetic differentiation, while their plumage differences help identify the two bestiary relatives.
sections.conservation: The 2023 global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern but records a decreasing population trend, with forest loss identified as a pressure across parts of its range.
